title: Estimated against actual rows: the sign that the statistics are wrong

videos.script: Every node of a plan carries two numbers once you run it with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. The rows the planner expected, and the rows that came. {{twonumbers}} When they agree, the plan was built for the data it met. When they disagree, it was built for some other data. {{disagree}} This lesson is about reading that disagreement. {{reading}} First, where to look. The error starts at one node, low in the tree, and every node above it inherits it. You read from the bottom and stop at the first node where the two numbers part. {{bottom}} Then, how it happens. A batch import adds three hundred thousand pending orders. The statistics still describe yesterday's table, where pending was a third of one percent. {{import}} The planner expects seven thousand rows and gets three hundred thousand. Above that scan it picks a loop instead of a hash, and a sort that spills to disk. {{cascade}} One ANALYZE later, the same query gets a different plan. {{analyze}} Last, what ANALYZE actually reads: a sample of thirty thousand rows, whatever the size of the table, and when autovacuum decides to take a new one. {{sample}}
